heading: Small fine-tuning sets can restore knowledge after unlearning
definition: a small relearning set (unrelated, loosely related, or a subset of the forgotten facts) restores the hidden knowledge.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce recovery from small relearning sets in models up to 10B parameters, including recovery of held-out facts. Success depends on the unlearning method and relearning data; unrelated data do not consistently work, and small-set recovery above 10B remains uncertain.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B: many independent groups across Llama, Mistral/Zephyr, Qwen, Gemma, Yi, OLMo and Phi (counts: versions.B.studies_by_size '1-10B': 83); the original group's own follow-ups at this scale (arXiv:2502.05209, arXiv:2407.15549, arXiv:2505.09500) count as R1 only. R2 at <1B for recovery in small from-scratch models (arXiv:2512.05648, arXiv:2506.06278, arXiv:2410.04332, arXiv:2607.08077; counts '<1B': 6). ? at 10-100B for the 'small set' wording. The only knowledge rows are a 250M-token SFT on MoE models in arXiv:2610.25791: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B, and Intern-S2, whose size is not stated. arXiv:2610.40751 uses the same SFT budget, and the first author of arXiv:2610.25791 is a co-first author of it. The behaviour rows on 32B models (arXiv:2609.38909, QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) split: ten deceptive forget pairs restore deception flags, but 100 steps on the model's own honest answers leave flags at 2.2% and 5.8% (r17, r18), which the checker reads as challenges, not limits_scope. counts '10-100B': 4. Not tested above 100B (no '>100B' key). R0 for toy networks: arXiv:2602.19215 (DNF networks) and arXiv:2605.01699 (a four-layer testbed of 810,496 parameters). In the testbed, after the paper's own edits, direct relearning on the secret returns it in 1-3 steps (2 for the unedited model). This relearning uses the full secret, with no never-trained baseline. Background domain text without the secret keeps P(secret) below 0.0026 over 50 steps (r22, challenges). Counts have no toy bucket.
suggested_status.reason:
The originals' own B results are thin. arXiv:2402.16835 reports that 8,000 Harry Potter sentences bring WHP close to the original on Familiarity (figure-only; no outcome for 800 sentences). arXiv:2403.03218 relearns RMU on Mistral-7B with the whole cyber forget corpus (figure-only). Groups that share no author with an original reproduce recovery from small or related sets, with controls:
- arXiv:2406.13356 (ICLR): relearn-only controls stay at 0% on TOFU and synthetic keywords and show no gain on WHP Rouge-L.
- arXiv:2409.18025 (TMLR): 5 forget examples take RMU 29.9 → 62.4.
- arXiv:2410.08827: held-out facts recover above 88%.
- arXiv:2505.16831 (ICML): Yi-6B, GA at LR 6e-6, N=100. Relearning on forget-set data at 10-100% of forget-set size restores forget-set F.Acc to 67.28-79.20 from 0.00 (original 78.90). Held-out scoring is not stated, so the relearned and scored facts may overlap.
The original group's own follow-ups count toward R1, not R2:
- arXiv:2502.05209 (TMLR) shares Ewart, Casper and Hadfield-Menell with arXiv:2402.16835, and its header flags this. One step on 64 examples gives more than 25 points for 6 of 8 methods.
- arXiv:2407.15549 shares five authors with arXiv:2402.16835.
- arXiv:2505.09500 shares Hadfield-Menell with arXiv:2402.16835.
The checks also find that arXiv:2408.00761 shares 7 authors with arXiv:2403.03218, that arXiv:2410.02760 shares an author (Samuel Marks) with arXiv:2403.03218, that arXiv:2410.12949 shares authors with arXiv:2402.16835, that arXiv:2610.26651 shares one author with an original source group (the checks do not say which), and that arXiv:2510.27629 shares five authors with arXiv:2403.03218 (WMDP). arXiv:2510.27629 has B rows but no B verdict, and it tests pretraining data filtering, not unlearning.
counts: versions.B.studies_tested 129, with verdicts.supports.studies 110, verdicts.limits_scope.studies 95 and verdicts.challenges.studies 24; tested_with_controls 112; tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 9. The studies index flags all nine SAME GROUP: the eight named above and arXiv:2508.06601 (index flag only; the checks name no overlap).
The challenges are tied to conditions, not to failed replications of standard-method recovery. The conditions are counter-methods, deep deletion, pruning, unrelated data, oracle-matched comparisons (arXiv:2611.00374 finds GA and NPO at the attacked oracle's level), and loosely related data for a behaviour target. In arXiv:2609.38909, 100 steps on the model's own honest answers leave deception flags at 2.2% (QwQ-32B) and 5.8% (R1-Distill-32B), r17 and r18. The checker relabels this group from limits_scope to challenges. The counts' verdict keys were built before the checks. So the challenges keys leave out this study and two more that the checker relabels limits_scope to challenges: arXiv:2610.21230 (benign Alpaca fine-tuning) and arXiv:2601.21702 (unrelated Wikitext). They still include arXiv:2510.00761 (NPO with ZO or Hybrid optimizers, relabelled limits_scope) and arXiv:2606.17168 (RepSelect under adaptive SVD-aware fine-tuning, relabelled none).
suggested_status.open_questions:
- Does standard-method recovery exceed an equally attacked never-learned or oracle model on WMDP-scale knowledge? arXiv:2611.00374 finds GA/NPO at oracle level on TOFU; arXiv:2512.05648 finds faster relearning at 254M.
- Why do thousands of in-domain documents leave Zephyr RMU/NPO near 35% in arXiv:2609.39866, when 5-60 examples restore them in arXiv:2409.18025 and arXiv:2502.05374?
- Does small-set knowledge relearning hold above 10B?
- Do TAR-style defenses hold across seeds and trainers (arXiv:2412.07097 vs arXiv:2408.00761)?
- Which unrelated or loosely related datasets recover which methods? Openwebtext and GSM8K recover; gibberish and Alpaca often do not; the model's own honest answers do not restore deception in arXiv:2609.38909.
- Would a group outside the original authors reproduce the original group's one-step, 64-example result (arXiv:2502.05209) and its few-example WMDP results (arXiv:2407.15549)?

source.title: eight methods to evaluate unlearning
source.authors: Aengus Lynch; Phillip Guo; Aidan Ewart; Stephen Casper; Dylan Hadfield-Menell

original_result.setup: The study used LoRA (low-rank adaptation) to fine-tune WHP, the Harry Potter unlearning model, on excerpts from the first three Harry Potter books.
original_result.result: The 8,000-sentence experiment used about 10% of the complete Harry Potter corpus and showed Familiarity, a measure of Harry Potter knowledge, only in graphs, without exact values. The Familiarity outcome for 800 sentences could not be determined.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

untested.basis: lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk's not-in-rows line says its SFT control is described but its results are not reported. arXiv:2502.05209's untested line says it has no comparison with a model that never learned the knowledge. The nearest case is arXiv:2508.06601 on 6.9B base models: WikiText fine-tuning leaves its data-filtered models unchanged on WMDP-Bio (R7, R8), while post-training CB on the unfiltered model 'rapidly becomes ineffective', which the authors confirm for CB and CB+LAT (R9, R10), all figure only. In these records its unrelated data is WikiText and its post-training arms are circuit breakers. Other controls in the packs cover forget-domain or related relearning (arXiv:2406.13356 R28-R30; arXiv:2512.05648 r1; arXiv:2611.00374 oracle; arXiv:2605.07482 Target) or TOFU retained data (arXiv:2601.22601), not unrelated SFT on WMDP.

wording_issues.issue: Many supporting results use large sets: 500-step SFT at batch 32-128 (2408.00761 untested-parts line), about 5,000 Bio texts in ELM's own test (2410.02760 r28 verdict fix), and 42,426 Pile-Bio Retain examples for 1000 steps (2412.07097 r20). Thousands of in-domain WMDP documents give only partial recovery: RMU Bio 34.83 vs 65.36 for the undefended model under the same attack (2609.39866 R46). Others in also use the full forget set, 628 facts, 250M tokens or a full removed corpus. Some methods need 25-75% of the forget set. Truly small sets do work elsewhere (5 forget examples, a 2-example batch, one step on 64 examples, ten deceptive pairs), but 20 samples × 1 epoch recover only partly, and several studies do not state set size. LUNAR on Llama-2-7B, PISTOL synthetic legal contracts: GRPO on forget-set prompts for 5 epochs raises pass@1 0.05 → 0.60 (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R3). No target labels are supplied, but the ROUGE reward is computed against forgotten answers. Training-set size and train/eval separation are unstated; the reward may teach some answers. This is verifier-guided RL evidence for recovery by fine-tuning, with small-set supervised relearning untested.

Recovery from unrelated data varies by method, model and data. It is near-complete with Openwebtext (Llama RMU WMDP-Bio 0.108 → 0.720 vs 0.710; 2411.12103 r49) and with GSM8K SFT (RMU 28.1 → 69.5%, base 73.2; lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk r11). It is absent with gibberish (GA WMDP MCQ 24.67% → 25.05%; Table 7 does not name the model, likely Zephyr; 2406.13356 R26). It is small with 1,000 Alpaca instructions: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct GD TOFU Forget Score goes from 19.32 at release to 20.98, against the study's TOFU threshold of 19.71, the mean recall on mismatched pairs (2610.21230 r37). Other studies split the same way. In toxicity, privacy, VLM and deception settings, unrelated or retain data mostly leaves the unlearned state in place.

Recovery falls off with relevance, and topic alone may not be enough. ROUGE-L recall on WHP GA is .4905, .3484 and .2916 for high-, mid- and low-relevance text, from .2910. The authors call even the high-relevance text 'only loosely related to the forget set' (2506.15699 R01-R03). On TOFU, a topically relevant set gives keyword RSR 0.0 at every relearning step from 11 to 47. A set that shares syntax with the target queries but holds no answers reaches 0.8 at step 23 (Table 7: 50 unlearning steps, unlearning method not named; 2602.03379 R5-R8, R10). Yet a general-biology retain set gives more than 25 points in one step on WMDP (2502.05209 R18). Related paragraphs without test answers also restore concepts strongly: RMU on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct goes from MC accuracy 22.8% after erasure to 70% after relearning (2606.03695 R31).

Recovery is often partial and sometimes overshoots. RMU, ELM, GA and RL recover 53-80% of the gap on Zephyr-7B (2505.04416 B1-B10). LLMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct reaches Cyber 27.6 → 41.3 and Chem 30.1 → 44.3 vs No Defense 46.4/47.8 (2408.00761 r8, r9). RMU PII P3 goes 0.00% → 18.32% vs a target of 60.60% (8dbe9be172e6f520f73ef4ba51b7bfbdc7f0d549 r23). GradDiff TOFU ES reaches 31.9 vs Original 26.7 (2609.36612 R1). Many results are figure-only or loss-only, so 'restores' often cannot be sized.

Only some studies compare with a model that never had, or had less of, the knowledge and is relearned the same way. One comparison is with data-filtered models: on a 254M model, RMU regains the no-filter baseline forget loss in 50 steps. Models pretrained without biology-labeled articles need 325 steps (weak filter) and 350 steps (strict filter); the paper says these filtered models may still hold some biology (2512.05648 r1). Relearn-only controls stay at 0% (2406.13356 R28, R29). Some unlearned models end at the reference level: GA and NPO reach ES 0.085 and 0.076, against 0.070 for the attacked oracle (2611.00374 T10-GA-ES, T10-NPO-ES). ESM-2 models never trained on viral data reach unfiltered-level performance after fine-tuning on it (2610.26651 R1-R12). Several studies have no never-learned comparison. Some gains come with general repair or reactivation from a reference model.

wording_issues.phrase: a small relearning set (...) restores the hidden knowledge
wording_issues.issue: The statement has no qualifier for unlearning method or depth, but recovery depends on both. NPO barely relearns in one TOFU setup, recovery AUC 0.068 (2601.22028 r5). Deep-deletion configurations revive 0.000-0.025 of held-out facts (2608.11408 R23, R24). Neuron pruning on Llama-3.2-1B, followed by fine-tuning on the benchmark train set, mostly leaves WMDP at 0.26-0.34. This holds for random and group-lasso pruning at 30/63/80% sparsity and for attribution pruning at 63/80%; for example, WMDP Bio after random pruning at 30% goes 0.22 → 0.27. The exception is attribution pruning at 30%, which the authors say achieves little unlearning: Bio 0.36 → 0.56 and Cyber 0.27 → 0.55, vs base FT 0.62/0.59 (2505.15811 R03, R07, R08). CIR leaves WMDP-Bio near random after a 100-epoch attack (2509.11816 r1). Full-parameter DPO, TAR, KUnBR, Hybrid-optimized NPO, Lethe, VKD and SimNPO are reported to reduce or resist recovery in their own setups.

wording_issues.phrase: a subset of the forgotten facts
wording_issues.issue: Subset relearning recovers held-out facts learned in pretraining, with recovery rates above 88% (2410.08827 r10-r18). It does not recover synthetic facts fine-tuned in after GD or RIA, below 35% (2410.08827 r20, r21), and the post finds no recovery on the corrected birthdays dataset (lw:9AbYkAy8s9LvB7dT5 r5). On CounterFact editing, no localization relearns more than 7% (2410.12949 r27).

Much of the evidence measures behaviours or non-LLM targets rather than LLM knowledge: toxicity (2602.23391 r25), deception flags (2609.38909), hallucination rates (2601.16527 r3), backdoor accuracy (2604.26809), and in also harmscore, robot skill success, image classes and concepts, KG facts and speaker identity.

method_sensitivity.factor: Relevance of the relearning data (forget subset > retain or loosely related > unrelated)
method_sensitivity.what: Recovery tracks how close the relearning data are to the forgotten facts. Yi-6B GA at a 30% budget: forget-set relearning far exceeds retain data (F.Acc 11.24) or unrelated data (6.48) (2505.16831 r18, r22). On synthetic names, English text ending with the target beats Japanese text (9%), female names (20%) and gibberish (9%) (2406.13356 R21-R23). ROUGE-L recall follows high > mid > low relevance, e.g. WHP GA .4905, .3484 and .2916 from .2910 (2506.15699 R01-R03). Ten toxic forget examples raise NPO toxicity 0.143 → 0.202 on GPT-2 Medium, while retain samples leave it at 0.148 (2602.23391 r07, r08).

method_sensitivity.factor: Unlearning depth, duration and learning rate
method_sensitivity.what: Deeper, longer or more aggressive unlearning often leaves less to recover, though not always. Revival is 0.800/0.695 for shallow GradDiff/RMU vs 0.025/0.000 for deep (2608.11408 R23-R26). On LKF with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, JensUn's relearnt score falls from 27.0 to 8.0 as unlearning grows from 200 to 2000 steps (WR 0.44-0.39). GradDiff goes 2.0 → 51.0 after 200 steps but 0.0 → 1.0 after 1000, which the authors put down to a broken model (WR 0.03). NPO recovers more after longer unlearning: 6.0 → 8.0 at 200 steps vs 10.0 → 26.0 at 2000 (2509.02820 r16, r20, r1, r4, r6, r10). On Yi-6B, an unlearning LR of 3e-5 cuts recovery to 41-61 from 72-80 at moderate LR for RMU/UnDIAL/AltPO/PDU (2505.16831 r35-r38). In CIFAR-10 diffusion with retain data, Salun recovers 0.647 (Plane) and 0.747-0.916 (other classes) after 10K unlearning steps, vs 0.187 and 0.373-0.813 after 20K. Yet Sfront, which has the largest generative loss, is the most recoverable (0.960-1) (2512.03564 O11, O16, O1).

method_sensitivity.factor: Relearning amount: samples, epochs, steps, learning rate
method_sensitivity.what: Larger sets, more epochs, more steps and higher learning rates recover more. NPO UE from 0.74: 20 samples × 1 epoch gives 0.57, 40 gives 0.39, 60 gives 0.37, and 20 × 3 epochs gives 0.37 (2502.05374 r1-r3, r8). NPO MUSE-Books KnowMem is 0.333, 16.525 and 34.126 after 50, 75 and 100 steps (2509.23362 B1-B3). RMU recovers at lr 1e-5 but changes minimally at 1e-6 (2504.08192 R7, R11). The EFUF rebound on mPLUG-Owl-7B grows with size: CHAIRS 50.5, 55.2 and 59.1 at 60, 100 and 140 samples (2601.16527 r3-r5).

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation metric, read-out and prompt type
method_sensitivity.what: The measure and prompt type change whether, or how much, recovery shows. The relearning-robustness score R is 0.43-0.70 on most metrics but 0.98 on Paraphrased Probability (2506.12618 r3, r4). After relearning, RMU on Zephyr rises on WMDP MCQ from 0.3086 to 0.4812 (fraction), while judge-scored answer completion moves only 1.89 → 2.24 (original model 5.92) (2406.13356 R15). Under maximum letter probability, fine-tuned unlearned models tend to recover base WMDP-Bio MCQ accuracy. Under maximum text probability that recovery does not hold, particularly for NPO (figure-only; 2506.00688 r9, r12). On Qwen2.5-VL3B after in-domain retraining, Mmunlearner at 50% of the forget set has a forgetting score of 15.67 on original prompts but 99.33 on paraphrased ones (higher means better forgetting). HFRU at 1% scores 38.67 on discriminative prompts vs 84.33 on original ones (2605.26992 r7, r12).

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack optimizer, relearning objective and which parameters are fine-tuned
method_sensitivity.what: How the attack is run matters. On LLaMA-3.2-1B, TOFU forget10, with forget+retain data for 1 epoch at lr 1e-4: SGD leaves every method, the gold model included, at its pre-attack ES. Adagrad takes RMU 0.035 → 0.597, NPO 0.085 → 0.208 and FRP 0.062 → 0.137. AdamW at that lr gives RMU 0.134, and Adafactor collapses utility (2608.25429 Table 11; no row in the pack; B verdict l2). For the same LLMU Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 and benign prompts, a KL objective raises harmscore 0.00 → 0.90 while gradient descent reaches 0.10 (2511.00030 r18, r15). SFT directly on REX-excised Qwen3.5-35B-A3B gives Bio 32.4% → 63.0%, vs 32.4% → 42.8% when SFT precedes excision (2610.25791 r36, r1). TAR recovery varies with seed, trainer, schedule, warmup, and LoRA vs full fine-tuning (2412.07097 r13, r15, r16).

Outcomes change with model size and family. OLMo3 7B resurfaces 0-23% of PII profiles vs up to 87% on OLMo2 1B (AlphaEdit email). The authors say it is unclear whether this is a property of the larger model or a limit of their resurfacing attack (2607.02513 R01, R05). Across RMU models from 61M to 1816M, the fraction of pretraining compute needed to recover shrinks with scale (2601.21571 r1, r21). Benign Alpaca gives Qwen GA 63.64 but Llama-3.2-3B GA 16.71 on FaithUn (2509.22263 F24, F3). ESM-2 recovery compute grows from below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M to 14-24 at 3B (2610.26651 R1, R5).

method_sensitivity.factor: Target domain and split (WMDP-Bio vs Cyber and other domains; known vs unknown forget set)
method_sensitivity.what: Recovery differs by target domain and split, not always in the same direction. LLMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct goes Bio 29.9 → 61.3 (No Defense 70.5) vs Cyber 27.6 → 41.3 (No Defense 46.4), so the Cyber ceiling is also lower (2408.00761 r7, r9). ELM on Zephyr-7B goes Bio 29.7 → 42.2 vs Cyber 27.2 → 29.4 (2410.02760 r28, r29). CIR on Llama-3.1-8B (0.1% disruption) runs the other way: Bio stays near random after the attack while Cyber recovers partly. Among Cyber questions the attack lifts, the longest option is correct 52% of the time vs 14% for the rest (2509.11816 r1, r4). TOFU PII P3 is higher on the known than the unknown split for all five methods, e.g. GA 26.19% vs 8.82%, NPO 38.10% vs 17.35%, RM 35.71% vs 3.53%. Model and attack budget are not stated for TOFU (8dbe9be172e6f520f73ef4ba51b7bfbdc7f0d549 r30, r31, r33).

method_sensitivity.factor: How the knowledge was acquired (pretraining vs later fine-tuning)
method_sensitivity.what: On Llama 3 (8b), facts learned in pretraining show recovery rates above 88% (2410.08827 r10-r18), while Random Birthdays facts fine-tuned in show below 35% for GD and RIA (r20, r21). The post reports no recovery on the corrected birthdays dataset (lw:9AbYkAy8s9LvB7dT5 r5).

method_sensitivity.factor: Unlearning method and the optimizer used to unlearn
method_sensitivity.what: Within one study and attack, the unlearning method decides the outcome. On Qwen2.5-VL3B, 1% of the forget set restores SLUG (95.67 → 13.00), while Mmunlearner and HFRU need 25-75% (2605.26992 r6, r7). Backdoor accuracy recovers to 90.74 after PGA and 88.52 after FedRecovery, but stays near 25 after FedEraser and FedOSD (2604.26809). For NPO on ICLM-7B MUSE-Books, the labelled Relearn100 results give KnowMem 0 → 45.2 with Adam, 0 → 31.3 with Hybrid and 23.9 → 33.2 with ZO (pre-unlearning 59.4). The rows' 34.8, 0 and 16.4 are Table A3's undefined 'W/ atk' cells (2510.00761 r7-r9). Relearning on the 500-sample OpenbookQA validation set lifts PO and SOPO on LLaMA2-7b by 24-31 points but O3 by +6.2 (2407.10223 F9 rows).

method_sensitivity.factor: Format, syntax and source of the relearning data
method_sensitivity.what: The form and source of the relearning data matter beyond topic. A syntactically similar set reaches keyword RSR 0.8 by relearning step 23 (cosine 0.7113, judge 0.9), while a topical set gives keyword 0.0 at step 11. Table 7 names no unlearning method (2602.03379 R10, R5). Matched unlearning and relearning formats need fewer samples (figure-only; 2506.00688 r5-r8). On Zephyr-7B-β with three WMDP folds, relearning on fold A and scoring fold B gives RMU 0.41 with MCQ data and 0.45 with corpus data, and L-RMU 0.40 and 0.49 (2505.09500 R05-R08). Unseen same-distribution examples recover less than retain-set examples (2505.22310 r8).
